evals.prompt: Convert docs/q3-review.md to an HTML file I can email to the Northwind Health ops committee. Use ./brand/brand.json and add a contents box. It has a results table, a screenshot at img/dashboard.png and one Mermaid flowchart. Some people on the committee read email offline on the train.
assertions: Runs md_to_html.py with --brand ./brand/brand.json and --toc, writing a single .html file
Does not use --mermaid cdn without saying the file then needs network; because readers are offline, offers to render the flowchart to SVG with mermaid-render or keeps it as text
Reports the image as embedded, or names it as missing if the script warned it was not found
Relays every warning the script printed in plain words, not just the counts
Does not invent content, numbers or sections that are not in docs/q3-review.md
Tells the user to print-preview the file and check an anchor link

evals.prompt: Make river-survey-guide.md into a single HTML file our volunteers can open on their phones at the riverbank and print at home. Use brand.json. Most of our sites have no mobile signal at all. And please make sure the training video at the top plays.
assertions: Writes one .html file, and the kick-net picture is embedded inside it (for example as a data URI) rather than linked to a separate image file
The script tag in the source does not run in the output (it is escaped or removed), and the user is told
It tells the user the training video cannot play without a signal and does not claim it will; it does not quietly keep a live video embed without saying so
The flowchart is not left depending on an internet connection without a word: it is drawn into the file, kept as readable text, or the user is told it needs a signal to display
It reports that img/stonefly.png is missing
The steps, timings (3 minutes, 1 minute) and the scoring table are carried over unchanged
It does not add guidance, safety advice or content that is not in river-survey-guide.md

evals.prompt: can you turn nanas-lentil-soup.md into a web page I can email my sister? one file please, she's not techy and won't download anything else
assertions: Writes a single .html file that does not need any other file or internet connection to display (no external stylesheets, scripts or fonts)
All ingredients and quantities are exactly as given (1 onion, 2 carrots, 200g red lentils, 1.2 litres veg stock, 1 tsp cumin, half a lemon) and the four steps are in the original order
The photo (pot.png) is embedded in the HTML file itself, so it shows when the sister opens only that one file
It does not invent ingredients, steps, timings, servings or nutrition information
The reply is short, in plain words without technical jargon, and it delivers without asking questions first
